Monsoon Flooding Inundates Media & Publishing Sites Across Myanmar, Disrupting Operations

YANGON, Myanmar, June 20 — Heavy monsoon rains have triggered widespread flooding across central and southern Myanmar, severely affecting the operations of media and publishing firms in the region, industry sources said Thursday. The deluge, which began early this week and is ongoing, has submerged printing plants, warehouses, and editorial offices, halting production and distribution of newspapers, magazines, and books.

At Shwe Inya Publishing’s main facility in Bago, floodwaters rose to over one meter on Wednesday, damaging printing presses and stacks of unsold newspapers stored on the ground floor. “We have suspended all printing activities since Tuesday night,” said Min Zaw, operations manager at Shwe Inya. “Some equipment is underwater. Our staff are safe, but many cannot reach the plant, and we have moved emergency supplies to the second floor.”

Industry association representatives estimate that at least 14 media and publishing sites in Yangon, Bago, and Mawlamyine have suffered partial or total flooding. “The situation is critical for our members,” said Daw May Thandar, spokesperson for the Myanmar Media & Publishing Federation. “Editorial teams are working remotely where possible, but most print runs are on hold and distribution networks are at a standstill. The full extent of the damage is not yet clear.”

Workers at several affected sites have been relocated to temporary shelters set up by their employers on upper floors. “We evacuated 18 staff from the ground floor and are providing food and water upstairs,” said Kyaw Lin, a supervisor at Golden Lotus Media House. “We are still monitoring the water level—it’s not receding.”

The flooding has also disrupted digital newsrooms, as some servers and archives stored on-site have been compromised by water ingress. “We’re worried about losing years of archives and raw footage,” said Yin Moe, an editor at Horizon News, which reported partial flooding of its server room.

Union officials have called on publishers to ensure the safety of their employees and to provide emergency pay during the ongoing disruption. “Workers are concerned about their jobs and health,” said Ko Aung Myint, a union representative.

With heavy rain forecast to continue, publishers are bracing for further disruption in the coming days.
